narrative: The reviewer's premise was correct on every one of the 48 findings, and the agent accepted all of them. 34 of the 48 trace to an earlier fix that was incomplete. Round 1's 22 findings are mostly twelve duplicate threads on one omission: the 964e815 helper comments claimed renderPriorFindingsBlock used severityTag/flattenBody when it still had its own oneLine and '(S${f.severity})'. Rounds 2-4 are a whack-a-mole over untrusted-path injection: backtick, then newline in the sweep bullet, then newline in the unanchored span, then lone \r, then the unshowable list and report heading. Only the e506b8a reply finally swept the whole class. Rounds 2 and 3 would still have run for findings left over from the original PR (F21/F28/F30, F32/F35), so only round 4 is strictly avoidable; the fix-caused share is far higher than that floor suggests.
guidance_observations: The agent's single wrong pushback (F4: trim is 'not expressible' in JSON Schema) produced F10 and then F43; a one-line pattern check would have avoided both.
Twice a reviewer named sibling sinks inside a finding (F7's second quoted phrase, F33's 'and in those lists') and the fix covered only the first, so the named remainder came back as new findings.
A 'closing the class, not the instance' sweep appeared only in round 4; doing it on F16, the first untrusted-path finding, would have removed most of rounds 2-4.
Writing comments that list a helper's consumers before migrating those consumers produced 12 duplicate threads in one round; grep each named consumer before committing the comment.
